independent: isolated codex exec; no sibling votes or Claude vote in context
reasons: The two cited lines are not clean false positives: each line goes beyond a status note and teaches the SCOTUS result/holding in Recent developments, including the later Chatrie v. United States / 609 U.S. ___ reference.

The proposed suppression uses a preceding circuit token as a proxy for subject court, but a real SCOTUS entry can naturally mention lower-court provenance before a bare SCOTUS tag, e.g. on cert from the 9th Cir. - SCOTUS held ..., so the tag-only true positive would be hidden.

Limiting the suppression to window[:tag.start()] does not solve the core ambiguity; it only proves a circuit reference appears before the tag, not that the first case is circuit-only or that no SCOTUS holding is being taught elsewhere on the line.
The fixture as described would encode the disputed examples as allowed even though N5's stated purpose says SCOTUS holdings belong in Key cases, not Recent developments.
residual_risks: Current 45-character-first-case window can miss a later SCOTUS case name, reporter cite, or holding language in the same bullet.
A bare Supreme Court reference remains intentionally exempt, so holding verbs plus a SCOTUS case name/cite later need separate detection rather than a broader tag suppression.
Scanning the whole line before the tag for circuit references would be even noisier because unrelated lower-court context could suppress a SCOTUS-tag violation.
suggested_tightening: Do not suppress solely because a circuit reference precedes SCOTUS. If metadata labels like 'superseded by SCOTUS' are allowed, suppress only that narrow status-label pattern after a classified circuit subject and only when the remainder of the line contains no SCOTUS case name, U.S./S.Ct. cite, or holding/result verbs; otherwise leave the HIGH active.
